content.value_statement: Small UI details often make finished products feel rough. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code review typography, surfaces, motion, and interaction polish.
actual_capabilities: Reviews nested border radius, shadows, image outlines, and hit areas for visual consistency.
Guides balanced headings, pretty text wrapping, font smoothing, and tabular numbers.
Recommends interruptible transitions, staggered entry motion, subtle exits, and contextual icon animation values.
Identifies broad transitions and unnecessary will-change usage in animation performance reviews.
Formats UI polish feedback as before-and-after tables grouped by design principle.
limitations: It provides guidance only and does not run automated visual tests.
It focuses on interface polish, not full product strategy or brand identity.
It assumes the project has frontend code, components, or UI requirements to review.
It does not replace accessibility, usability, or cross-browser testing.

use_cases.title: Polish A React Component
use_cases.description: Review a component for radius, shadows, motion, typography, and hit area issues before release.

use_cases.title: Standardize Design System Details
use_cases.description: Align surface treatment, animation behavior, and typography details across reusable components.

use_cases.title: Make UI Feedback Actionable
use_cases.description: Turn subjective feedback into concrete before-and-after implementation changes.

prompt_templates.title: Review One Component
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this component for UI polish. Return a before-and-after table grouped by principle.

prompt_templates.title: Improve Motion Details
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit these animations for interruptibility, entry timing, exit timing, icon transitions, and page load behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Polish Surfaces And Type
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these styles for radius, shadows, image outlines, optical alignment, text wrapping, smoothing, and tabular numbers.

prompt_templates.title: Perform A Full Polish Pass
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill across the provided frontend files. Group every change by principle in concise before-and-after tables.

output_examples.input: A card uses the same radius on the outer container and inner image.
output_examples.output: The review recommends a larger outer radius and smaller inner radius so nested surfaces look concentric.

output_examples.input: A toolbar icon appears on hover and switches instantly between two states.
output_examples.output: The review recommends cross-fading opacity, scale, and blur so the icon state change feels smooth.

output_examples.input: A dashboard counter shifts horizontally when values update.
output_examples.output: The review recommends tabular numbers so each digit has equal width and the layout stays stable.

best_practices: Apply the guidance during implementation, then verify the result in the running interface.
Use the before-and-after table format so each change stays concrete and reviewable.
Pair this skill with accessibility checks for focus states, contrast, keyboard support, and reduced motion.
anti_patterns: Do not use it as a replacement for user research, accessibility testing, or requirements.
Do not apply every animation rule when the interface needs a calmer static experience.
Do not add dependencies only for an animation suggestion when CSS can solve it.

faq.question: What work is this skill best for?
faq.answer: It is best for polishing frontend components, product screens, and design system details.

faq.question: Does it generate complete UI designs?
faq.answer: No. It reviews and improves interface details in existing or planned frontend work.

faq.question: Can it work with Tailwind and React?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance includes Tailwind, CSS, React, and motion library examples.

faq.question: Does it require Framer Motion?
faq.answer: No. It recommends motion libraries only when the project already uses them.

faq.question: What output format does it prefer?
faq.answer: It asks for before-and-after tables grouped by design principle.

faq.question: Is it a testing tool?
faq.answer: No. It provides review guidance and should be paired with visual and accessibility testing.
